course_name_original: Mecánica y teoría de mecanismos i
course_name_en: Mechanics and Theory of Mechanisms I
prerequisites: FUNDAMENTOS FÍSICOS DE LA INGENIERÍA II/20224005 (PHYSICAL FUNDAMENTALS OF ENGINEERING II)
FUNDAMENTOS MATEMÁTICOS DE LA INGENIERÍA I/20224006 (MATHEMATICAL FUNDAMENTALS OF ENGINEERING I)
MÉTODOS NUMÉRICOS Y PROGRAMACIÓN ALGORÍTMICA/20224003 (NUMERICAL METHODS AND ALGORITHMIC PROGRAMMING)
FUNDAMENTOS FÍSICOS DE LA INGENIERÍA I/20224004 (PHYSICAL FUNDAMENTALS OF ENGINEERING I)
FUNDAMENTOS MATEMÁTICOS DE LA INGENIERÍA II/20224007 (MATHEMATICAL FUNDAMENTALS OF ENGINEERING II)

learning_outcomes.text: Applies the principles of theory of machines and mechanisms.

Recognizes and identifies the equilibrium conditions of a solid or set of solids in the plane and in space. Understands and uses different Kinematic analysis methods and applies them to a planar mechanism.

syllabus_topics: 1. Introduction to Classical Mechanics.
1.1. Particle Mechanics.
1.2. Mechanics of Systems of Particles.
1.3. Rigid Body Mechanics.
1.4. Cases of Conservative Forces: Potential Energy and Kinetic Energy.
2. Rigid Body Statics.
2.1. D'Alembert's Virtual Work Principle in Static Equilibrium in 2D and 3D.
2.2. Application of Newton-Euler Static Equilibrium Equations.
3. Statics of a System of Rigid Bodies.
3.1. D'Alembert's Virtual Work Principle in Static Equilibrium of a System of Solids in 2D and 3D.
3.2. Application of Newton-Euler Static Equilibrium Equations to a System of Solids.
4. Adhesion in a System of Rigid Bodies.
4.1. Cases of Non-Conservative Forces: Coulomb's Model.
4.2. D'Alembert's Virtual Work Principle in Static Equilibrium of Solids in 2D considering adhesion.
4.3. Newton-Euler Static Equilibrium Equations applied to solids in 2D considering adhesion.
5. Introduction to Machines and Mechanisms.
5.1. History, Generalities, and Definition of Machines and Mechanisms.
5.2. Classification, Representation, and Schematization of Mechanisms.
5.3. Mobility Criteria for Mechanisms: Kutzbach-Grübler Criterion.
6. Introduction to Rigid Body Kinematics.
6.1. Introduction to Kinematics in 2D and 3D.
6.2. Kinematics Applied to Machines and Mechanisms: Study of Positions, Velocities, and Accelerations.
teaching_methods: Introductory activities (Course presentation and evaluation criteria).
Lectures (Development of main theoretical concepts using ICT and blackboard).
Problem-solving/exercises in the classroom (Exposition of acquired concepts by detailed problem solving).
Personalized attention (Resolution of doubts and explanation of unachieved concepts).

assessment_methods.method: Homework exercises to be solved in pairs during the 2 hours of problem class
Written test of theoretical concepts and exercises (First test)
Written test of theoretical concepts and exercises (Second test)

assessment_rules: For the first call, the average of the two development test grades must be 4 or higher to be combined with other continuous assessment grades. Additionally, the minimum grade for the second development test must be 4.0 or higher for it to be averaged. For the second call, the exam accounts for 80% of the grade, combined with 20% from homework problems, provided the final exam grade is 4 or higher.
